newsitem.title: USA: Summers - Clinton to maintain balance budget effort.
newsitem.headline: Summers - Clinton to maintain balance budget effort.

text.p: The second Clinton administration will continue to strive to balance the U.S. budget, promote education and training and push for freer trade, Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said Wednesday.

"We're going to move towards a balanced budget, we're going to keep investing in America," Summers said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television the morning after President Clinton was reelected to a second term.

Addressing Clinton's economic priorities for the second term, Summers said the administration would concentrate on "creating room for more investment by our businesses in equipment," as well as investments in technology, training, education and opening more markets.
"Those are the pillars of prosperity," he said. "They've been working for the last four years. We're going to keep going -- balancing the budget with investment and with opening markets."
On trade, Summers singled out China's markets as a top priority for the administration.
"No question about it, market opening with China, which is now responsible for our largest bilateral deficit, will be something that will be an important priority ...," he said.
In dealings with Japan, Summers said it "should be possible" for trade negotiators to complete their insurance talks by their December 15 deadline.
While declining to answer questions on the dollar or U.S. monetary policy, Summers said the dollar's health is affected more by the U.S. economy than by a planned European currency.

"If we focus on our fundamentals, if we have a strong economy, I think the dollar will do just fine," he said. "Obviously we'll be watching closely what happens with 'Big Euro,' but I don't think there's going to be any replacement for the U.S. dollar in the world economy."
Summers said a prosperous European economy is in the U.S. interest since Europe is a major consumer of U.S. goods. He said the U.S. economy's potential for growth can be expanded.

"We can grow this economy as fast as our potential allows us, and what we've got to do is work on increasing that potential," Summers said. "And that's why investments are so important, that's why educating our people is so important, why focusing on technology is so crucial."
